content.text:
MathJax supports `\color` and `\textcolor` for coloring the distributions.

MathJax likely does not support TikZ-style `blue!60` syntax. Hex colors matching the TikZ palette will be used instead.

The best approach matches the figure legend style. Plain text labels will use `<span style="color:#5c8fd6">` and `<span style="color:#d62728">` for the Binomial and Poisson colors. Inline math expressions will use `\textcolor{#5c8fd6}{...}` and `\textcolor{#d62728}{...}`.

Finalized exact hex codes: `#5b8fd4` for the Binomial label and `#e03131` for the Poisson label. Considering whether to wrap the entire phrase in raw HTML spans, since kramdown may not render inline math correctly inside HTML elements.

Using a single `<span>` for the whole phrase avoids awkwardness. Kramdown should handle the inline math inside it. Alternatively, MathJax `\textcolor{#5b8fd4}{...}` and `\textcolor{#e03131}{...}` would be cleaner.

The drafted sentence uses `\textcolor{#5b8fd4}{\text{Binomial pmf}}` and `\textcolor{#e03131}{\text{Poisson}(\lambda)\text{ pmf}}`. The original text says "pdf" rather than "pmf", but I will leave it unchanged because the user only asked for colors. I am also considering whether simple HTML spans would better match the figure caption's reference to "blue bars" and "red dots".

Settled on inline HTML spans for readability. Reusable CSS classes were rejected as unnecessary for a single line. Checking the obsidian-to-distill skill for color conventions.
